runners_data.name: Ballystone
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for John McConnell who handles Good ground (won on similar), has form over today's trip, and holds a place chance if the leaders tire; 92 days off is a minor flag but McConnell tends to target his horses fresh at Galway festivals.
runners_data.comment: Gained a winner two starts back but has been unplaced on his latest outing, and 92 days off the track is a fitness query; he has experience of today's going, though a struggling trainer and a big weight of 166 lb make this tough.

runners_data.name: Glens Sensation
runners_data.note: 171 days off the track is a serious concern, and the history of fading in the finish makes this distance over fences a tough ask; naturally a hold-up type but has shown no form on Good ground across five sampled runs, making meaningful involvement hard to project.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pull-up and an unseating among recent efforts, Glens Sensation has been off for 171 days and faces a stiff task ranked last on our figures here; he has run over today's trip and going before, which is at least some footing to build on.

runners_data.name: Great Attitude
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner who won over fences on Soft and was placed on Good; Ricky Doyle rides and the horse's style fit in this race is near-perfect — sole pace-setter against a field that will respect the early lead, though the drop from that winning trip is a minor consideration.
runners_data.comment: Great Attitude showed a fine turn of foot when winning three starts back, and his going experience holds him in good stead, but 136 days off the track is the obvious question mark against him on his return.

runners_data.name: Mickie Angel
runners_data.note: Hogan-trained eight-year-old who likes to race prominently, and the two recent placings on Good and Heavy give encouragement; his true style is front-rank but the pace dynamic in this field pushes him into a midfield role he won't relish, so his finishing effort may come from a less advantageous position than his form suggests.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Mickie Angel faces a stiff ask here; the 166 lb burden won't help, though he has run over today's trip and going before, and placed finishes last time and three starts back show he can hit the frame.

runners_data.name: Ocastle Des Mottes
runners_data.note: Paul Townend takes the ride for Mullins, which is the headline angle — the OR-126 horse has Good-ground form and placed at this sort of trip before; a prominent racer whose jumping will need to be cleaner than the P last time, but Mullins/Townend at Galway is always a live factor.

runners_data.name: Talk In The Park
runners_data.note: Shaped prominently throughout his career and has two wins and five places on Good-ground variants making him well-suited to today's conditions; headgear (p) suggests he has needed help to concentrate, and Keith Donoghue's record in Galway staying chases gives this runner a genuine live chance in a pace scenario that suits front-rank types.
runners_data.comment: Finished second three starts back and was fifth two starts back, Talk In The Park has experience over today's trip and going and arrives here fresh after 53 days off; the concern is that pulled-up effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Themanintheanorak
runners_data.note: The six-year-old won on Heavy and has placed on Good, but his recent string of 6th-place finishes on Good at 2m4f-3m suggests he struggles to pick up when the gallop is honest; a natural front-runner by inclination, he is being mapped back into midfield by the competitive pace shape, and that mismatch must temper expectations significantly.
runners_data.comment: Themanintheanorak landed a win in his last five starts but has since posted three consecutive sixths, and 81 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 116 keeps him competitive mid-division.

runners_data.name: Vicar Street
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the mount for Mullins — second string to Ocastle Des Mottes in stable terms but Cobden is not here to make up numbers; OR-120 with a win and three places from four Good-ground starts is an outstanding going profile, and the 2m4f win on Good at Galway itself (sim-going record: 1W3P from 4) marks this horse out as the standout course-and-conditions performer in the field.
runners_data.comment: Placed in each of his last three starts — third last time out, second two starts back — Vicar Street clearly has consistency going for him, though his win three starts back came before a subsequent dip in form; he returns after 55 days off carrying 166 lb and has experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Wendrock
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott five-year-old who is still learning his trade over fences — the P and 0 in recent form are jumping concerns — though he placed on Good and the headgear (p) may help sharpen his jumping; a natural hold-up runner who needs the race to pan out very specifically, and as a young horse still finding his feet over fences, each race brings uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Wendrock nevertheless heads this field on our ratings and arrives on a manageable 31-day break with experience of today's going; the weight burden of 166 lb is the one factor to monitor.

runners_data.name: Seventy Eight Team
runners_data.note: Carries a 7lb claimer (Conor Clarke) and the lowest weight in the field; the OR-79 is well below the class standard here, and while the sim-going record shows a place on Good at marathon distances, nothing in the form suggests he can compete at this level — makes the numbers.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up in each of her last two starts, Seventy Eight Team arrives after a 55-day break carrying 159 lb and ranked second-bottom on our figures — a combination that makes her very hard to fancy, though she has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Great Attitude is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival looking to press for the lead, should coast into an uncontested, rhythm-dictating position from the off over this 2m6½f trip on Good ground at Galway. Ocastle Des Mottes, Talk In The Park, and Vicar Street are all prominent-running types who will want to sit just behind, creating a compact early group but without the pressure that would stretch or collapse Great Attitude's gallop. The field actually holds more prominent-minded horses than the race shape can accommodate — Themanintheanorak and Mickie Angel are natural front-rank types who are likely to be shuffled back into a midfield role they don't naturally want, reducing their effectiveness. This race shape — a controlled, honest pace with a lone leader and a cluster of prominent trackers — most favours genuine prominent-to-tracked-leader profiles who can travel sweetly and attack the final fences, particularly those with strong Good-ground form and proven stamina at this trip or beyond.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Great Attitude Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Great Attitude bowls along uncontested and sets a fair, sustainable gallop that the trackers cannot disrupt.
scenarios.body: Great Attitude dictates terms from the front, the race staying truly run without being a sprint, and the prominent chasers sit in a tight pack just behind; when the fences come thick and fast in the final mile, horses who have travelled smoothly in behind the leader and can quicken off a sound pace will be best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Land Late Power
scenarios.trigger: If Great Attitude's steady gallop compresses the field and a prominent tracker produces a sustained jumping run over the final circuit to collar the leader.
scenarios.body: A moderate pace kept by Great Attitude allows the prominent chasers to float along without burning energy, setting up a genuine test of jumping accuracy and stamina from the third-last; horses with the best recent form and class, positioned just off the pace, can stretch away from those who have been unable to get their natural position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Outjump Tired Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves deceptively strong over the final circuit and the lead group tie up, allowing hold-up horses to arrive late.
scenarios.body: Great Attitude's lead unravels approaching the last and runners who have been covered up midfield get a run through beaten horses; genuine hold-up types such as Ballystone and Wendrock, who have natural late-race energy, could profit if the ground rides more testing than the Good description suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos At Fences Reshuffles Race
scenarios.trigger: If significant jumping errors or fallers in the prominent cluster cause wholesale positional changes in the final mile.
scenarios.body: The pack of prominent runners tracking Great Attitude — all competing for limited space on a turning track — creates the conditions for a loose horse or a faller to interrupt the race flow; surviving hold-up horses or a recovering prominent type may inherit winning positions late, with Talk In The Park's steeplechase experience an asset in such a scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch Themanintheanorak and Mickie Angel at the start — both are natural front-runners pushed into unnatural midfield roles; if either forces their way to the front to contest Great Attitude's lead, the pace dynamic changes entirely and the prominent-tracker scenario dissolves.

Glens Sensation's 171-day absence combined with a tendency to fade in the finish is a significant welfare and race-integrity watch — monitor its jumping from the second circuit and flag any signs of distress.

Vicar Street's outstanding Good-ground record (1W3P from 4 runs) makes it a strong pace-shape beneficiary, but Harry Cobden riding the apparent Mullins second-string is a notable booking that suggests connections may see it differently — any drift in the market is meaningful information.

Great Attitude's jumping accuracy is the crux of the whole race — as an uncontested leader over 2m6½f on a turning track, any significant error at a fence could allow the prominent cluster to swamp it before it can recover, immediately triggering Scenario B or C conditions.

Ocastle Des Mottes pulled up last time and Paul Townend's booking implies Mullins expects a forward showing — watch its jumping from the early fences closely, as a second jumping failure would confirm the P was a fitness/jumping issue rather than a one-off.

runners_data.name: Jalila Moriviere

runners_data.name: Ballybawn Belter
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride for Liz Doyle, who has had just one runner in 14 days; 118-day break is a concern, and his form figures show a tendency to fade at the business end on soft, though three placings on similar-going types offer some hope.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out is the positive to hold onto, but Ballybawn Belter hasn't won in her last four starts and returns after 118 days off carrying 154 lb. She has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 131 suggests she's competitive at this level.

runners_data.name: Littlefoot
runners_data.note: Visor in the headgear, won over exactly this trip on Good ground recently and again on Soft — the sim-going record is solid at 10/15; Sam Ewing keeps the ride and the 21-day turnaround is a positive sign of wellbeing.
runners_data.comment: Littlefoot showed his best when winning two starts back, but a pulled-up effort last time out is the obvious concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and 21 days gives fair prep time, though carrying 154 lb tests his stamina.

runners_data.name: Intense Approach
runners_data.note: Bit-wearing front-runner type whose Good-ground record is strong (4W5P in similar going) but recent form includes two pulled-up runs and a fall; 29 days since last run and the big field at Galway complicates his jumping.
runners_data.comment: Intense Approach won five starts back but has since failed to recapture that form, with an unplaced effort last time out among three consecutive poor returns; experience over today's trip and distance is a plus, though a struggling trainer (0/22) and 153 lb are tough asks.

runners_data.name: Kings Hill
runners_data.note: Placed twice in the last three runs including on Good, and the 11-day turnaround suggests a trainer who fancies him; no wins yet on Good but four placings in similar conditions and JJ Slevin is a major positive in a race like this.
runners_data.comment: Kings Hill brings solid recent form — a winner three starts back, third two starts back, and runner-up last time out — and has run over today's trip and going before, but 153 lb is a stiff burden and an eighth-of-22 ranking suggests he faces stiffer opposition here.

runners_data.name: Yoradreamer
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins partners this Mullins-trained mare who has gone 1-2 in her last three completed efforts on Good or similar; the 21-day break is fine, though she fell on Good ground at this trip in her most recent start — jumping confidence to monitor.
runners_data.comment: Yoradreamer was second one start back from a pulled-up latest, but has shown ability, including a win four starts back; he has run over today's trip and going, though ranked 13 of 22 on our rating, he faces a stern test under 153 lb.

runners_data.name: Moonovercloon
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type who has run 13 of his last 15 on Good or similar and rarely wins (no wins on Good in recent history), but the apprentice Kenneally is weight-saving; needs a strong pace to exploit from off it and that may not fully materialise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 14th of 22 in the field, Moonovercloon has experience of today's trip and going but a return of unplaced, seventh and fourth in recent outings offers limited encouragement, and 152 lb is a stiff burden after 46 days off.

runners_data.name: A Penny A Hundred
runners_data.note: Brian Hayes aboard this Mullins hold-up runner whose form string of 3470-7 is uninspiring; stays well but the 7/25f and 12/26f on soft suggest he finds this trip tough in good-ground conditions where the pace will be steadier.

runners_data.name: Shanbally Kid
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy cannot mask the form line — four PUs in recent history and the system flags a tendency to fade in the finish; nine-year-old who handles Good ground but the 151lbs weight and deteriorating form make him hard to trust in a 22-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and has pulled up twice and unseated in that sequence, Shanbally Kid arrives on a going he has encountered before and 21 days fresh, but his jumping reliability is a serious concern that outweighs his 131 rating.

runners_data.name: Rising Dust
runners_data.note: Six wins and nine placings in 15 similar-going runs is a standout stat in this field; Emmet Mullins yard has had a runner in the last 14 days, the horse is a natural prominent who jumps well and has won at this distance on Good — the profile fits the dominant scenario clearly.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts give Rising Dust some profile, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but back-to-back eighths in his most recent outings make him very hard to fancy, and our figures rank him last of the 22 runners here.

runners_data.name: Where's My Jet
runners_data.note: Paul Townend takes the ride but this horse's record on Good is weak (1W2P) and recent form reads 060P-0; a natural prominent who has consistently failed to land a blow over the past season, and nothing in the data suggests a reversal today.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up two runs back, Where's My Jet arrives on 53 days off carrying 150 lb, which is a stiff ask; he has run over today's going before, though, and a rating of 129 suggests some residual ability to exploit.

runners_data.name: A Law Of Her Own
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins has this mare back after 289 days off — the longest absence in the field — and though she won last time out over 16f on Good, the step up to 2m6½f and the ring-rustiness after a near-ten-month break are serious questions; she is a natural prominent who will find it hard to assert in a congested race.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 289 days is the chief concern here, and she ranks near the foot of our assessments in this field; that weight of 149 lb adds further pressure. She has run over today's going before, and a win last time out at least brings some recent winning form to the table.

runners_data.name: Baltic Bird
runners_data.note: Consistent placing record on Good (3W5P in similar) and ran just 13 days ago suggesting fitness; a natural front-runner by style who has been mapped to midfield given the crowded prominent division — his chance is tempered by the likelihood of racing further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Baltic Bird has been winless in his last five starts, though a third three starts back offers some encouragement; his two most recent efforts — eighth and sixth — suggest he's struggling to recapture that form, and 149 lb is no help.

runners_data.name: Donnie Devito
runners_data.note: Four consecutive third-place finishes on Good ground give him strong each-way claims; genuinely prominent by style but mapped to midfield given the traffic — if Shane Markey (7lb claim) can thread him through to a handy spot, the consistent placing record makes him competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 18th of 22 on our figures, Donnie Devito faces a stiff ask here; he has been consistently placed in recent starts, though, and has run over today's trip and going before, with 28 days between runs suggesting he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Hermino AA
runners_data.note: Won his last start over 25f on Soft and handles Good; a natural front-runner who will find himself further back than he wants in this field, with only 6 of his last 15 runs on similar going — the redistribution to midfield genuinely compromises his winning chance.
runners_data.comment: Hermino AA was a winner last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, giving him every reason to strip fit off a 53-day break — the main concern is whether the 148 lb burden blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Warriors Wood
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has won and placed consistently on Good (3W6P in 10 runs), and the 14-day turnaround is positive; natural prominent type mapped to midfield, but youth and consistency on this going make him one of the more interesting of the redistributed group.
runners_data.comment: Warriors Wood has finished fourth and third in his last two starts, with his sole recent win coming three starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, and returns on a quick 14-day turnaround, but ranked 16 of 22 on our figures, he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Antrim Coast
runners_data.note: Five placings in last five completed runs including two seconds on Good — arguably the most consistent horse in the race; Darragh O'Keeffe is an experienced handler of big-field chases and though he races out of his natural prominent position, he has the form to be involved.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Antrim Coast has been runner-up three times in that sequence — most recently a second three starts back — but back-to-back defeats in sixth and fifth suggest a dip in form; he has run over today's trip and going, though 147 lb is a stern ask.

runners_data.name: Rexem
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type with a solid recent second on Good at 20f; ran just 7 days ago which is the shortest turnaround in the field — fitness is assured but fatigue risk is real in a 2m6½f stamina test; placed in four of five recent Good-ground runs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 17th of 22 on our figures, Rexem faces a stiff task here, with his trainer yet to land a winner in 22 attempts over the last fortnight; experience over today's trip and going, plus a second last time out, are the only crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Charlie Luciano
runners_data.note: Won over 26f on Good last time out and has the strongest going-specific record for a hold-up type (14/15 similar going); Noel Meade has been in decent form (3/13 in 14 days) and Conor Stone-Walsh keeps the ride — the stamina profile suits a strong pace.
runners_data.comment: Two pulled-ups in recent starts make him hard to trust despite a last-time-out win, and he ranks 19th of 22 on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, but 145 lb adds another obstacle.

runners_data.name: Lord Lariat
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old with the oldest profile in the race and a form line that reads 00F8P- over the last six runs; bit and tongue-tie worn, 90 days since last run, and nothing in the recent record suggests he can compete at OR 119 in a 22-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five and pulled up most recently, Lord Lariat does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and our rating of 132 suggests he retains more ability than his official mark of 119 implies — the concern is a stop-start recent record that makes him hard to trust.

runners_data.name: El Champo
runners_data.note: Trainer Rothwell has had two wins from 31 runners in 14 days; genuine front-runner by style displaced to midfield, and recent form figures include two PUs and a 9th — even if he gets forward as his natural style demands, the form does not encourage confidence.
runners_data.comment: Two pulled-ups in recent starts make El Champo hard to fancy, and he's winless in his last five, ranked 21 of 22 on our figures; a return after 54 days adds to the queries, though he has run over today's trip and going, and a third five starts back offers a distant crumb of comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Addragoole is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 22-horse field and, with no rival likely to press hard from the flag, should dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over the 2m6½f trip on Good ground at Galway. Behind him, a cluster of genuine prominent types — Jalila Moriviere, Ballybawn Belter, Littlefoot, Intense Approach, Kings Hill, Yoradreamer and Rising Dust — will battle to settle just off the pace, creating a reasonably strung-out mid-race shape rather than a bunched, falsely-run affair. The field holds significantly more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; of those redistributed to midfield on the map, Donnie Devito, Baltic Bird and Warriors Wood are the most likely to actually push forward and find a spot closer to the pace than their mapped position suggests. A controlled pace set by one genuine front-runner over a stiff staying trip on Good turf is a scenario that historically favours horses who can travel prominently without burning energy early, then sustain their effort into the final climb — prominent types who jump well and stay the distance are the profile to follow here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Addragoole Dictates, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Addragoole sets an honest but uncontested gallop and the race is run to suit strong stayers finishing out the trip.
scenarios.body: Addragoole controls the tempo from the front, leaving prominent rivals to race in a compact group behind him before the race stretches late; horses who travel smoothly in second or third and jump economically get first run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Hold, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely sustainable and a hold-up horse produces a strong finishing run off the back of a solid gallop.
scenarios.body: A steady but honest pace set by Addragoole allows a well-positioned hold-up type to creep into contention from midfield turning for home and collar the leaders on the run-in; the Good ground rewards a clean, sustained finish rather than a sprint.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types crowd the early pace, lift the tempo, and the front two pull clear as the field ties up behind.
scenarios.body: Addragoole and one prominent rival who secures a handy position — likely Jalila Moriviere or Yoradreamer — find themselves in front of a ragged, effort-spent field entering the final mile; a two- or three-length advantage at the last proves decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Wide Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the big field produces traffic trouble and a horse from an unfavoured position delivers a winning run wide of rivals.
scenarios.body: With 22 runners negotiating Galway's fences, fallers or interference cause gaps in the midfield pack and a horse who bypasses trouble on the outer arrives fresh in the straight; the winner comes from an unexpected position.

watchPoints.text: Warriors Wood, Baltic Bird and Donnie Devito are all natural prominent types who will push forward from their mapped midfield positions — watch for crowding and bumping at the early fences as they attempt to assert, which could unseat or block better-fancied rivals.

Shanbally Kid has a history of pulling up and the system flags a tendency to fade in the finish — in a 22-runner field over fences, a weakening horse in the middle of the pack is a serious interference risk for those tracking behind.

Addragoole's 112-day absence and top weight of 167lbs mean his stamina over the final mile is uncertain even if he controls the early tempo — watch for him to be swallowed up approaching the last two fences, potentially causing a sudden shift in momentum across the field.

A Law Of Her Own returns from 289 days off and, as a prominent type, is likely to race enthusiastically early before her fitness is tested — monitor her jumping closely in the first mile as a fresh, under-raced horse jumping at speed in a big field is a classic fallers' scenario.

Rising Dust's exceptional going record (13/15 on similar going, 6 wins) means he is the benchmark for how the race should pan out — if he fails to travel prominently as expected, the pace shape has likely broken down and the race is more open than it appears.

races.name: Guinness Handicap

runners_data.name: Shaool
runners_data.note: Progressive hold-up performer for JP Murtagh, two recent wins at 10f on Good/Yielding; stepping up to 1m4f for the first time here is the key question but breeding and style suggest it will suit, and this pace map is ideal for a late finisher.
runners_data.comment: Shaool has back-to-back wins in her recent form and she has run over today's trip and going before, with our rating putting her at the head of this field — but three consecutive poor runs since those victories make it hard to know which version turns up today.

runners_data.name: This Songisforyou
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner; Emmet Mullins handler in good recent form, but at age 8 and with a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting she often races more prominently than a true leader, the risk is she finds the solo lead position unfamiliar at this level.
runners_data.comment: Ran a fine second last time out and returns after just over a month looking primed for this trip and going, This Songisforyou carries 140 lb yet remains winless in recent starts — though that placed effort hints he's close to landing one.

runners_data.name: Dawn Rising
runners_data.note: Veteran of nine campaigns, placed at 1m4f on Good before; inconsistent recently with an 8th last time, and at OR 98 is weighted to perform without showing obvious upward trajectory — needs something to go wrong for others.
runners_data.comment: Dawn Rising has experience over today's trip and going, and that second in his last five starts — five runs back — gives him a foundation to build on; our ratings rank him second of 18 in the field, yet winless in recent starts and a current run of poor finishes make him a significant ask.

runners_data.name: Chica Guerrera
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4-year-old filly for Mark Fahey with a 7lb claimer; has been placed four times in five runs and all recent form is at 10f, so this 1m4f trip is a step into the unknown, though the steady pace might help her see it out.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 15 of 18 on our figures, Chica Guerrera faces a stiff ask, though she does arrive off a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going before; 41 days off the track and 133 lb on her back make her hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Port Of Spain
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien 3-year-old wearing a hood; OR 102 is the highest in the field, but recent form shows a string of mid-pack finishes and 44 days since last run — needs the extra class to translate over a trip he hasn't fully proven.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Port Of Spain does at least have going experience to call on and was third four starts back, though a return from 44 days off and 131 lb to carry make further progress hard to guarantee.

runners_data.name: The Real Screamer
runners_data.note: Won twice recently at 10f and 12f in good style; Paul Flynn handler in decent form with T14 at 3/19, and the prominent style suits tracking This Songisforyou — one of the most naturally placed horses in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Ranked well down the field on our figures, The Real Screamer faces a stiff task, though he arrives in decent nick — third last time out and a winner two and three starts back — and has experience of today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Fixation
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride for JP Murtagh stable; won at 10f on Good last time and has front-foot form, making the prominent tracking role very natural — the 1m4f trip is a step up but style and recent form make this an interesting contender.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 18 on our figures and carrying 130 lb, Fixation is hard to fancy despite winning last time out; the trainer's current 4% strike rate — one win from 24 in the last 14 days — adds little encouragement, though he has going experience in his favour.

runners_data.name: Touch The Moon
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes booking for William Durkan; won at 1m6f earlier in the season so stamina is confirmed, but recent Good-ground form has been mixed and a trainer with 0 wins from 7 over 14 days is a minor flag.
runners_data.comment: Touch The Moon won three starts back and was runner-up two starts back, but has drifted to fourth last time out; he has distance and going experience in his favour, though carrying 130 lb could prove the key test here.

runners_data.name: Kingstonian
runners_data.note: 68 days since last run is notable; Joseph O'Brien handler but a lengthy absence and the prominent style (with a hood) means he needs to find his race quickly — his 1W3P on similar going over today's trip suggests the conditions are right if fit.
runners_data.comment: Kingstonian showed smart form when second and third in consecutive starts, but a ninth-place finish last time out raises questions, and 68 days off the track adds an element of doubt; has run over today's trip and going, though his 129 lb burden is no help.

runners_data.name: Mo Ghille Mar
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won at 17f on Good earlier this season; John Joseph Hanlon handler, and while the form figures show inconsistency (05196-), the strong staying profile and closing style fit the predicted slow-run race less well than a true end-to-end gallop.
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back but sixth last time out, Mo Ghille Mar has distance and going experience in her favour and 29 days off could have her fresh; however, her trainer is badly out of form at 1/21 recently, and a mark of 88 makes life tough off 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Tribal Star
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner by nature whose true style could not be accommodated in this overloaded prominent group; Adam Caffrey rides and recent form is modest (443902), and racing out of his natural position reduces his chance materially.
runners_data.comment: Tribal Star is winless in his last six starts but has placed second most recently and third four starts back, showing he's capable of hitting the frame; he has experience over today's trip and conditions, yet consistency remains the concern from a 128 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Mr Vettori
runners_data.note: Shane Foley for Jessica Harrington; 3-year-old with a hood, 69 days off the track, and all best form over shorter trips of 8-10f — the step to 1m4f is significant and the long absence creates additional uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Thread Of Gold
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins 3-year-old with two wins from four starts on Good ground; lightly raced and unexposed at this trip, which is a notable extension from his 9f best — if he stays, the hold-up style and Mullins/Lee combination make him a serious factor.
runners_data.comment: Thread Of Gold won last time out and was seventh three starts back, and that inconsistency in form makes him hard to fancy ranked 13 of 18 on our figures; going experience counts in his favour, though.

runners_data.name: Immutable
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Joseph Murphy who was a true prominent racer forced into a midfield slot by the congested pace group; an 89-day break is a significant concern and his best Going-ground form came at shorter, making this assignment difficult on multiple fronts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 89 days off, Immutable does have distance and going experience to call on, and our rating of 97 suggests he holds more ability than his official mark of 85 implies — though that layoff may blunt his chance on reappearance.

runners_data.name: Navy Waters
runners_data.note: McCreery handler, wearing a visor; genuine front-running type who loses his place in the queue here — four of five recent runs have been placing efforts so the ability is present, but racing off his preferred early position costs him significantly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, though a third three starts back offers a crumb of encouragement; Navy Waters has distance and going experience to call on, but carrying 125 lb off a mark of 85 makes her task no easier after 33 days off.

runners_data.name: Night Moon
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins hold-up horse who won last time at 1m4f on Good — the most recent run is an obvious positive; the 49-day gap is manageable for this yard, and Slattery takes the ride, though a redistribution into midfield means his natural closing position is still achievable.
runners_data.comment: Night Moon has won two of his last four starts and arrives here having run over today's trip and going, but ranked bottom of 18 on our figures, he faces a stiff ask against this field despite his recent winning form.

runners_data.name: Satono Chevalier
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old for MK Flannery ridden by a 3lb claimer; three wins from recent starts including at 10f and 13f, but a true prominent racer who is squeezed out of position — the style displacement at this age and with an amateur combination makes recovering hard.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom two on our figures and that speed rating of 69 makes him hard to fancy, though he does bring distance-and-going experience plus a third last time out; the gelding has shown winning form in recent starts but is up against it here.

runners_data.name: Narlita
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for H Rogers with Siobhan Rutledge up; all handicap form has been at 8-12f on soft or heavy ground, making today's 1m4f Good surface a question on two counts — a genuine front-runner who cannot get her position and faces an unsuitable surface profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Narlita did show a flash of form with a third three starts back, yet a sixth two starts back and a fourth last time out — 41 days ago — suggest she remains frustratingly inconsistent; she has run over today's trip and going, but her rating edge may not be enough to bridge the gap.

races.paceDynamic: This Songisforyou is the confirmed front-runner and, with a clear lead in a field of 18 on Good ground at Galway over 1m4f, she should dictate at a sustainable, uncontested gallop that neither burns off the pace horses nor stretches the hold-up brigade prematurely. The field is overloaded with prominent-running types — Tribal Star, Navy Waters, Immutable, Satono Chevalier, and Narlita are all genuine front-to-midfield horses who cannot all get their natural position and will be shuffled back, compromising their chance. This Songisforyou will likely have Chica Guerrera, The Real Screamer, and Fixation tracking closely, with the bulk of the field strung through midfield under a controlled pace scenario. The tactical verdict is clear: a lone leader setting a honest but unforced gallop on Good ground over 1m4f at Galway favours hold-up horses with a strong turn of foot who can be produced wide off the home bend — genuine closers with Good-ground form at this trip are best placed to benefit from the predictable pace shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Over The Top
scenarios.trigger: If This Songisforyou sets a steady, sustainable gallop and the race only quickens in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The controlled early pace compresses the field and leaves plenty of fuel in the tank for late finishers, allowing Good-ground hold-up types to sweep past a tiring pace group.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a close-tracking prominent horse sits second or third and kicks decisively off the final bend.
scenarios.body: This Songisforyou's unforced gallop allows one or two handy types to sit in a perfect stalking position and have first run on the field turning for home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and This Songisforyou is never challenged, stealing a lead that no one can close.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling pace at Galway can turn 1m4f into a sprint finish from which a horse that has led throughout and conserved energy benefits enormously.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Aids Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed prominent types contest the early positions more fiercely than expected, injecting genuine pace that blows up the front rank.
scenarios.body: A more contested gallop than the map suggests would exhaust the leaders and expose the genuine hold-up horses, allowing the furthest back to come from a winning position.

watchPoints.text: Thread Of Gold has won twice on Good ground and the Mullins/Lee combination is in sharp form — if this unexposed 3-year-old stays the 1m4f trip, his hold-up style is perfectly suited to pouncing late off This Songisforyou's steady gallop.

Shaool has won two of his last five on Good ground and JP Murtagh knows the track well — watch whether Rory Mulligan (5lb claim) can get a position just off the pace to allow a sustained late run, as the trip step-up looks the only doubt.

This Songisforyou's lone lead is sustainable in theory but her STYLE_FIT flag suggests she may not hold the position comfortably under pressure — if Chica Guerrera or The Real Screamer crowd her early, the tempo could lift unpredictably.

The cluster of redistributed prominent types (Tribal Star, Navy Waters, Immutable, Satono Chevalier, Narlita) all want to race up with the pace but cannot — watch the first two furlongs for jostling, which could create an uneven early gallop and tighten the margin between Scenario A and Scenario C.

Port Of Spain is the top-rated runner at OR 102 but carries a hood and was held up at longer odds in his last start at 1m4f on Good — Wayne Lordan's judgement of how to place him in a field this size will be decisive, given his profile needs a moderate pace to excel.

races.name: Arthur Guinness Handicap

runners_data.name: Casamorati
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who has faded in the finish in all four recent starts, all on Good ground, with no win or place from back-end positions — J P O'Brien yard has a strong 15/68 14-day strike rate but this one is flattered by the map.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Casamorati has experience over today's trip and conditions, yet his recent run of eighth, ninth and eighth tells against him; at 140 lb from stall 3, he'll need a career-best to get involved from fifth in our ratings.

runners_data.name: Only One Scobie
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with one win from 13 attempts on Good ground, finishing 13th twice at this course's parent surface — limited form in this going context and a fade-in-finish concern compounds the wide draw risk in a big field.|
runners_data.comment: Returned unplaced last time but was third two starts back and a winner three starts back, giving his recent form a mixed look; he has run over today's distance and going before, though 140 lb from stall 16 are factors to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Sweet Baby Zou
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up runner who won over 10f on Good last time out, so the step up to 1m½f is not a concern — 56 days off and the O'Brien yard's volume of runners tempers confidence, but the distance profile is the most interesting angle here.|
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back but unplaced last time out, and 56 days off adds a fitness query; she has experience of today's trip and going, though her speed rating of 63 leaves her with plenty to find against the top-rated runners from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Femme Beauty
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has won twice on Good ground including over longer trips, giving her a strong staying profile for this distance — the amateur jockey Danny O'Leary (10lb claim) is a factor to watch but the horse's consistent recent form and natural position just off the pace suits this race shape very well.|
runners_data.comment: Femme Beauty won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but a 39-day absence and a stiff 139 lb from stall 19 are real tests of whether she can back that up at this level.

runners_data.name: Good Man Jack
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with only three runs, none on Good ground with success, and a best finish of 7th — insufficient evidence to rate highly and the fade-in-finish flag reinforces a cautious view.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a seventh and ninth among recent efforts, Good Man Jack arrives here ranked last on our figures and carrying 139 lb from stall 18 — he has run over today's trip and going before, but there is precious little in the form to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Hassaniya
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the field, wearing headgear (tongue-tie, t/p), with placed form in two of five runs on similar ground — controls this race from flag to finish if allowed a free lead, and the absence of any pace rival is the defining tactical fact of this card.|
runners_data.comment: Hassaniya has been knocking on the door with back-to-back thirds in recent starts, and he has experience over today's distance and going. Carrying 139 lb from stall 20, our rating of 85 marks him as the one to beat, though he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: In The Gloaming
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has run prominently in prior runs but showed only fifth-place efforts over shorter trips on Good — stepping up to 1m½f is a significant test and the lack of a win or place on this going is a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, In The Gloaming has at least shown consistency with consecutive fifth-place finishes, and has run over today's going before; the 139 lb burden from stall 15 makes life harder for a gelding yet to find the winner's enclosure.

runners_data.name: Down The Glen
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose best form came in heavy-end going (wins on Heavy and Soft) — Good ground here is a clear reservation, and 57 days since last seen means fitness must be assumed rather than confirmed.|
runners_data.comment: Down The Glen showed smart form when winning earlier in the sequence and has experience of today's distance and going, while our rating of 77 ranks him second of 21 runners — a strong threat. The main risk is a 57-day absence combined with an unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Mr Perth
runners_data.note: Unknown style (style=U), holds a fade-in-finish flag, and has been off 77 days — three runs only, none resulting in a win or place on Good ground, and his form figures of 8-7-10 give little encouragement at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked 17th of 21 on our figures, Mr Perth faces a stiff task here; 77 days off the track raises freshness doubts, though he has run over today's trip and going before and stall six is a neutral draw.

runners_data.name: Tharaka
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map position by the volume of rear-runners in this field; long 305-day absence since last run is the dominant concern here — even with Emmet Mullins' angle, the layoff and the style displacement discount this runner meaningfully.|
runners_data.comment: Twice a fourth and placed third in recent starts, Tharaka has run over today's trip and going and her rating of 76 marks her as a serious player from stall 12 — the concern is 305 days off the track leaves her fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Belle Nuit
runners_data.note: Natural back-of-field runner whose true hold-up role cannot be accommodated in this shape; four runs include a best of 4th on Soft and a string of double-figure finishes on Good — ground and crowding both work against her.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Belle Nuit does bring going experience to the table and 23 days between runs leaves her reasonably fresh; however, consecutive unplaced efforts head into this, and carrying 135 lb from stall 2 makes the task no easier.

runners_data.name: Aquilla Star
runners_data.note: Placed twice in ten career runs, including a second over 10f on Good which is the best distance-going match in her form; mapped to midfield though a true hold-up type — the 11-day turnaround is tight but the trip suits better than most of her recent assignments.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15th of 21 on our figures, Aquilla Star faces a stiff ask, with her trainer yet to land a winner in 22 attempts over the past fortnight; experience over today's going is the one gentle positive.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Funk
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent mid-division finishes including a second over 8f on Heavy — the step up to 1m½f is a question but the horse races off a low enough mark and secures a good tactical berth just off the pace in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Cosmic Funk ran a solid second three starts back and returns here on a retrieval mission just 16 days later, with experience of both today's trip and going working in his favour — the main concern is that he's been winless in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: John La Bear
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Standard and has placed twice, but his true hold-up style is absorbed into midfield here because of the field's back-heavy configuration — Good ground form is limited and the tactical displacement is a genuine handicap.|
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back but has been below that level since, and with a speed rating of 54 he faces a stiff ask against 20 rivals; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, though 134 lb from stall 8 is no easy proposition.

runners_data.name: Jp's Express
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best run (3rd, 8f, Good) is the only notable piece of form; the 3lb apprentice claim from Wesley Joyce is a minor positive but the style fit score of 0.90 flags meaningfully that this horse will struggle to operate from its natural position.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with two unplaced efforts among them, Jp's Express is hard to fancy on these figures — ranked 18 of 21 in the field. A return to form third last time out offers slim encouragement, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Snaafy
runners_data.note: Strong form on Standard/AW surfaces including a win over 8f, but only two runs on Good ground and both ordinary — a true hold-up horse bumped into the midfield map, which tempers confidence despite the Declan McDonogh booking being a positive pointer.|
runners_data.comment: Snaafy hasn't won in his last four starts, and ranked 20 of 21 on our figures he faces a stiff task here; second last time out offers a crumb of comfort, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but the weight of 134 lb doesn't help his cause.

runners_data.name: Aurora Mist
runners_data.note: Trainer-ridden (Andrew Slattery trains and rides) which is an unusual pairing at this level; won over 8f on Good earlier this season which is solid form, but a true hold-up runner displaced into midfield in this crowded shape — the 16-day return is fine.|
runners_data.comment: Aurora Mist won two starts back but has been unplaced on her most recent outing, and ranked 16th of 21 on our figures she faces a stiff ask here; the experience over today's trip and going, plus a 16-day turnaround, at least count in her favour.

runners_data.name: Love Orchid
runners_data.note: Unknown style runner carrying a hood (blinkers) for Noel Meade, who has three winners from 13 runners in the past 14 days — the Meade angle is worth noting, but five runs on Good have brought no win or place and the form figures 4-6-9-5-4 show consistency at the wrong end.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Love Orchid nevertheless drops a shade in class on our rating and has run over today's trip and going before; the 133 lb burden from stall 13 is the chief concern for a filly who has yet to threaten the frame in recent outings.

runners_data.name: Priorstown
runners_data.note: Unridden (no jockey listed), off 84 days, and a true hold-up horse redistributed into midfield — three runs only, best a 6th on Heavy ground, and the absence of a rider declaration at this stage is a significant market question.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and returning after 84 days off, Priorstown has experience of today's distance and going but his trainer is struggling badly at 1/24 over the past fortnight, which tempers any claims despite our rating of 72 suggesting he holds a little more ability than his official mark implies.

runners_data.name: Ella's Gold
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with placed efforts in five of eight career runs including a second over 7f in similar going — no jockey listed but the horse's style profile sitting just off the pace is ideal for the dominant scenario, and the OR of 61 gives handicap upside.|
runners_data.comment: Ella's Gold has shown consistent placing ability, finishing second three times and third once in her last five starts, though she remains yet to win in recent form. She has run over today's trip and going before, and 31 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Dont Get Me Wrong
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won over 7f on Standard ground — Good ground and the longer 1m½f trip are both untested, and the style displacement into midfield in such a crowded field reduces the chance of this runner finding its natural rhythm.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 19 of 21 on our figures, Dont Get Me Wrong has been out of the frame in his last three starts — seventh, ninth, and eighth — and it's hard to look past that slump despite him having run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Hassaniya is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 21-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — she should be able to roll along at a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without ever being pressured into a suicidal pace. On Good ground over 1m½f at Galway this is a potent position: dictating the fractions, conserving energy through the home turn, and quickening on her own terms. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types and midfield runners, but the redistribution flags on Tharaka, Belle Nuit, Snaafy, Aquilla Star, John La Bear, Jp's Express, Aurora Mist, Priorstown and Dont Get Me Wrong reveal the true congestion — many of these are natural rear-of-field horses who simply cannot access their preferred position in such a large, pace-thin field, meaning the pack behind Hassaniya will be dense and messy rather than organised. Prominent types Femme Beauty, Cosmic Funk and Ella's Gold should secure a decent vantage point just off the leader, which is the most advantageous real-estate in this shape. This race shape unequivocally favours the prominent/close-tracking profile: with one sustainable gallop set from the front, horses racing in the first five to seven will have first run on the closers who will face a wall of traffic from deep in the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hassaniya Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Hassaniya leads unchallenged and sets a measured pace that suits horses tracking just off her.
scenarios.body: Hassaniya controls the fractions comfortably and the race unfolds at a tempo that keeps the strong closers bottled up in traffic; horses positioned prominently get the clearest passage turning for home and use the momentum off the bend to score. Femme Beauty, who has won twice on Good ground and stays this trip well, and Ella's Gold, a consistent placer with prominent tactics, are ideally placed to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Steals It Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled pace Hassaniya sets is slow enough that she never faces a genuine challenge and simply outstays the field.
scenarios.body: With no pressure from behind and Good ground that rewards relaxed, economical front-running, Hassaniya can effectively turn a handicap into a solo time trial, arriving at the two-furlong pole with a lead the crowded pack behind cannot claw back. Her recent placed form at this trip on similar ground makes a front-to-finish success genuinely plausible in a race with no pace rival.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just brisk enough to stretch the field and create gaps for a well-positioned midfield horse to pick through.
scenarios.body: A slightly stronger tempo than Scenario A means the field strings out more on the home turn, opening lanes for a horse sitting sixth to tenth who can quicken on Good ground; Cosmic Funk's consistent prominent-to-midfield profile and course-relevant form make it a candidate, while Snaafy — though a natural hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield map position — has the class shown by its form figures to capitalise if a gap materialises. The caveat is that redistributed horses like Snaafy are racing out of their true role, tempering confidence in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail, Chaos Decides
scenarios.trigger: If the large field produces significant traffic problems late and the race is won by whichever horse avoids the carnage.
scenarios.body: With 21 runners, the bulk of whom are genuine hold-up types forced into a compressed mid-pack, the closing straight at Galway could become a logjam; the winner in this shape would likely be a horse who found unexpected early cover just inside the leaders rather than a true late-closer. True hold-up horses like Casamorati or Good Man Jack are the profile that benefits on paper, but their fade-in-finish flags and redistribution context make this the least reliable outcome.

watchPoints.text: Hassaniya goes unchallenged to the lead — if she bowls along uncontested at an honest-but-not-fast pace, she could be very difficult to peg back from the front and punters holding prominent racers should watch the opening quarter-mile for any signs of a surprise pace challenger emerging.

Femme Beauty with the amateur rider — Danny O'Leary's 10lb claim is an asset in weight terms but watch whether he can place the filly promptly from whatever draw she gets in a 21-runner field; losing the prominent position would be costly in this race shape.

Traffic hazard in the home straight — with the majority of 21 runners compressed into a mid-to-rear pack behind a single front-runner, the straight at Galway will be congested; horses drawn wide or with riders who can split gaps (Gary Carroll on In The Gloaming, Ben Coen on John La Bear) may gain a material advantage.

Priorstown has no jockey declared — monitor final declarations closely, as a last-minute booking or a non-runner could alter the field dynamics and race weight distribution slightly at the tail of the market.

The redistributed cluster (Tharaka, Belle Nuit, Snaafy, Aquilla Star, John La Bear, Jp's Express, Aurora Mist, Dont Get Me Wrong, Priorstown) — nine true hold-up horses are all racing out of their preferred position; if any one of them finds a surprisingly clear passage, it will be the beneficiary of luck rather than tactical execution, making the winner from this group hard to identify in advance.

runners_data.name: Celtic Druid
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a win on Standish-type ground and solid course form at similar trips; McCourt yard 1-from-8 in 14 days is modest but horse's own form string (114732) is the key selling point, and 1m6f on Good looks well within compass.
runners_data.comment: Celtic Druid has placed last time out and was third two starts back, but ranked 19 of 21 on our figures, he looks up against it here; the experience over today's trip and going offers some consolation, though 140 lb is a stern burden.

runners_data.name: Lady Plimsoll
runners_data.note: Four months off the track is the main query, but prior form shows placed efforts at 1m4f-2m on Good and Soft; prominent style suits the likely race shape and O'Callaghan has a runner from 8 starts in the 14-day window — keep fit-to-race assumption modest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but has placed twice in that sequence and brings solid each-way claims here as the top-rated runner; she has run over today's going before, and third last time out and a second two starts back suggest she retains form, though 123 days off will need to be overcome.

runners_data.name: Tatum
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's runner is a natural prominent type flagged as the de-facto front-runner here, yet the STYLE_FIT tag (0.91) signals it is racing out of role; 8 days since last run and a decent Good-ground record (3W from 10 sim-going runs) are positives, but the out-of-role concern must temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Tatum arrives on the back of a win last time out and a victory five starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour. Carrying 140 lb after just eight days' turnaround is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Baila Conmigo
runners_data.note: Ran just yesterday — significant fitness flag — and has zero wins from three Good-ground attempts in similar company; prominent racer at 69 OR who looks overworked at present, with the 1d turnaround the dominant concern.
runners_data.comment: Baila Conmigo won last time out and has going experience in his favour, but his two wins in his last six starts are offset by a fifth two runs back, and 139 lb is a stern ask for a gelding ranked 14 of 21 on our ratings.

runners_data.name: Hexagonal
runners_data.note: Recent winner (OR 69) over shorter, but all career form is over 7f-10f and this 14f trip is a stamina leap; prominent style could see it feature early, but the headgear note and trip-extension make this a speculative staying qualifier.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win last time out, but six days is a quick turnaround and he's been inconsistent in recent starts, with four finishes outside the placings in his last six. Has run over today's going, and 139 lb is no featherweight.

runners_data.name: Steps In The Sand
runners_data.note: Veteran 7yo whose sim-going record (13 runs, 3W 4P) is strong on Good, but has been running over extreme distances (18f-22f) and drops back slightly in trip here; prominent style suits but the form string includes a 12th and a 9th recently — needs things to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Steps In The Sand showed she could compete when second four starts back and a winner five starts back, but three consecutive unplaced efforts since tell against her. She has experience over today's trip and going, and 19 days since her last run suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Goin'
runners_data.note: Hold-up racer for AJ Martin over trips around 2m plus, and this 1m6f may be slightly short of his best; has only two placed efforts from 11 Good-ground runs, and without a strong pace to aim at he risks getting no run.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and third four starts back, Goin' has shown consistency without a win in his last five starts, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the 138 lb burden is the key concern for a gelding operating off a mark of 68.

runners_data.name: Trubshaw
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's 4yo is a genuine prominent racer with course-form placed efforts and a win at 14f on Good, but the field's pace glut means it is mapped to midfield against its nature; Gabriella Hill takes a 7lb claim — the style dislocation is the main tactical drag here.
runners_data.comment: Trubshaw won four starts back but has finished sixth, unplaced, and eighth in his last three, making recent form the concern; he has run over today's trip and going, and an eight-day turnaround keeps him fresh, though 138 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Cooley's Mist
runners_data.note: Won last time over 13f on Good and has placed efforts at similar trips; a natural front-runner whose prominent instincts will be frustrated by the crowded early stages — Hayes in the plate is a positive, but the horse needs to find its rhythm from a position it won't naturally occupy.
runners_data.comment: Cooley's Mist arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's distance and going, yet he sits mid-pack on ratings and carries 136 lb, which may blunt his recent momentum.

runners_data.name: Mr Rango
runners_data.note: Ageing 8yo hold-up type whose best recent run was a 2nd at 17f; needs a strong pace to deliver and this race may not supply it — the lack of a win from 7 Good-ground attempts is a concern, though the trip suits.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six, Mr Rango nonetheless showed real quality when second two starts back, and a rating of 74 among a 21-runner field marks him as a leading threat; the risk is that last-time-out ninth leaves his consistency open to question.

runners_data.name: Quiz Test
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer with three placed efforts at 14f-17f on Good, but Shane Foley cannot magic the horse to the front when there are six others ahead of it in the queue; 51 days off and the blinkers flag are secondary considerations to the positional squeeze.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, Quiz Test at least brings distance and going experience to the table, and a speed rating of 76 hints at ability — though 51 days off and a hefty 136 lb burden are the key questions to answer here.

runners_data.name: Blackjack Hills
runners_data.note: Won twice as a 3yo, but all recent form is over shorter trips (8f-12f) and Good ground returns a modest 0W 1P from seven runs; hold-up style over 14f here on Good means it needs everything to go right.
runners_data.comment: Backed up a recent second with a win three starts back, but ranked 20 of 21 on our figures and a seventh two starts back undermines confidence; going experience at least gives him a foothold.

runners_data.name: Coulstys Way
runners_data.note: Placed in four of five runs at 14f on Good, making this a horse with genuine trip affinity, but is another natural prominent type who will find its preferred spot blocked; the 16-day break and lack of a win from 11 Good-ground runs moderate enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15th of 21 on our figures, Coulstys Way faces a stiff task here; third last time out and a second four starts back offer faint encouragement, and she has run over today's trip and going before, returning on a fresh 16 days.

runners_data.name: Nancee Spain
runners_data.note: Showed ability at 2yo/3yo level with wins on Soft, but the Good-ground record is thin (0W 1P from four attempts) and a hold-up style in a slow-run 14f race limits her viability; blinkers noted.
runners_data.comment: Nancee Spain has run over today's trip and going, and a win four starts back shows she can find the line — but her last three runs have all been out of the frame, and that dip in form is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Bell Ex Too
runners_data.note: 3yo at OR 70, all form over 10f-12f and no win from four career starts; prominent style but the form (6576) is uninspiring and the step up in trip to 14f is unproven — low probability runner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Bell Ex Too arrives 20 days fresh and has run over today's going before, but a string of mid-pack finishes — sixth, seventh, fifth, sixth — and a speed rating of 60 suggest he faces a stiff task off 129 lb against a field of 21.

runners_data.name: Vantage Code
runners_data.note: Ben Coen's booking is an upgrade for this 3yo who has placed twice on Good at 10f-12f; prominent/handy racer who stays well enough, though the headgear-h flag and only modest OR 69 suggest it needs the race to set up rather than finding it.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and second two starts back, Vantage Code shows consistent placing ability in recent starts, though winless in his last five and a return just four days ago raises freshness questions; has run over today's going, and 128 lb is workable at this level.

runners_data.name: Blissful Bonita
runners_data.note: Cromwell's 3yo filly has placed on Soft at 12f but Good-ground form is bare (0W 0P from three attempts); listed as a prominent racer though the field's excess means she'll be further back, and at 42 days off the form fitness question adds another layer of doubt.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with finishes no better than second in that spell and a trainer currently in the depths of a lean spell (1 from 35 in the past fortnight), Blissful Bonita — ranked 17th of 21 on our figures — faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Espritroyale
runners_data.note: Another Cromwell 3yo, hold-up style at trips around 10f — this 14f test on Good is the longest the horse has faced and there is no evidence of staying power; 41 days between runs and modest form (0W 0P on Good) make this low priority.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 18th of 21 on our figures, Espritroyale faces a stiff task, with the trainer in poor nick at 1/35 over the past fortnight; second last time out is the one genuine positive to cling to.

runners_data.name: Lauro's Legend
runners_data.note: Carries a notable "fades in finish" flag which is damaging in a 14f stamina test; the last three outings read 7-0-0 and the trainer (Fahy) has zero winners from four runners in the 14-day window — a hard horse to back on any front.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked 16th of 21 on our figures, Lauro's Legend has little recent form to recommend him despite experience over today's trip and going; the 134 lb burden adds further pressure on a gelding who needs to rediscover his best.

runners_data.name: Out On Friday
runners_data.note: A decade-old handicapper who ran 2nd at 10f on Good last year but whose recent efforts show 7th, 14th, 11th and 15th; a natural hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map — the form says this is a very tough ask at OR 63.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, though he did post a second three starts back to show he's capable of mixing it; seventh last time out, 15 days ago, keeps him relatively fresh, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Covert Legend
runners_data.note: Consistent placer (four 4ths in recent starts) but has never won in 15 Good-ground appearances and his true hold-up style is shown on the map in midfield by redistribution; at OR 63 he may fill a frame position but the no-win record on Good is a structural ceiling.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with four fourths and a second three starts back, Covert Legend faces a stiff task here — ranked last on our figures, though he has experience of today's going and returns after a 27-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Tatum is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 21-runner field and, critically, is flagged as racing out of role — this is a horse mapped as Prominent that will be pushed to lead by circumstance rather than genuine front-running inclination, meaning the pace it sets is likely to be sustainable and unforced rather than truly punishing. Behind it, the field is saturated with genuine prominent-types — Trubshaw, Quiz Test, Cooley's Mist, Coulstys Way, and Blissful Bonita are all natural front-runners or prominent racers who cannot all secure their preferred position in a 21-runner handicap, and several will be squeezed back into midfield against their wishes. That compression of pace in the early stages — too many horses wanting to be forward, most failing — creates a scenario where the race is likely run at a controlled, steady tempo with a single largely uncontested leader and a bunched midfield that will produce a messy, attritional finish rather than a truly fast-run contest. In a slowly-run or evenly-paced 1m6f Galway handicap on Good ground, the tactical verdict is clear: horses with genuine stamina who can race handy or make a smooth move from mid-division are favoured, while true hold-up horses dependent on a strong pace to bring them into play are at a structural disadvantage given how many in this field will clog the midfield without ever igniting a genuine gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tatum Controls, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tatum bowls along uncontested and the compressed prominent brigade fails to close, leaving a steady-gallop that rewards those who travel handy into the straight.
scenarios.body: Tatum sets an untroubled lead at a fair clip and the field strings out through the middle miles; horses who can race within two or three lengths of the pace and sustain their effort up the Galway straight hold the key tactical edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Squeeze Turns Chaotic
scenarios.trigger: If the overloaded prominent group creates early friction and mid-race crowding, elevating the pace and burning out the leaders.
scenarios.body: The excess of prominent-types jostling for position forces a faster-than-expected tempo through the middle of the race, tiring the forward horses and opening the door for those able to track the pace without being involved in early scrimmaging.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swooop Late
scenarios.trigger: If pace genuinely quickens due to early friction and the closers find clear daylight in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop than the lone front-runner alone could generate — created by the prominent squeeze — sets up a stronger finishing run from hold-up types; with a good passage, late finishers can get into it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Tatum dictates an even slower, crawling pace and the field bunches so tightly that the leader simply cannot be caught off an uncontested lead.
scenarios.body: A true dawdle suits Tatum's uncontested position even if it is not a natural front-runner, with a slow early pace allowing it to conserve energy for a long, drawn-out sprint home that bunched mid-division rivals cannot organise themselves to peg back.

watchPoints.text: Monitor the early stages for a positional battle involving Trubshaw, Quiz Test, Cooley's Mist, and Coulstys Way — if all four press forward simultaneously they will force a significantly stronger pace than Tatum alone would set, fundamentally changing the race shape from steady to genuinely run.

Baila Conmigo ran just yesterday and Steps In The Sand has questionable recent form — if either horse shows early distress or drops away unusually quickly in the first mile, it signals the pace has been set too high for the field's collective fitness level.

Tatum's jockey Paddy Harnett (5lb claim) faces a complex task managing an out-of-role front position in a 21-runner field — watch for whether it is allowed to bowl along uncontested or whether pressure arrives within the first four furlongs, as that distinction determines which scenario plays out.

Goin' and Mr Rango are the truest hold-up horses in the field — if they are still in double-digit lengths of the leader approaching the home turn it is a strong signal the pace has been slow and the race will be decided in the final furlong by those already positioned close to the action.
