runners_data.name: Counting Coup
runners_data.note: Showed placed form on soft at 13f and won over similar in season, but here he is a genuinely prominent-natured horse who will struggle to secure that position with Uxmal and Galileo Dame ahead of him — his recent 4th at Galway on Good (12f) offers some course form but the redistribution from his natural spot tempers his chance materially.
runners_data.comment: Counting Coup arrives here a winner two starts back and goes on today's going, giving him plenty to work with off 135 lb; the main risk is that his most recent start since that victory ended in a fourth, suggesting he can be inconsistent.

runners_data.name: Taipan
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with his best recent form (win at 14f, Good) now 89 days ago; the layoff is a concern for Mrs Harrington's runner, but he is a legitimate hold-up type and the Good going matches his winning conditions — market support off this absence will be telling.
runners_data.comment: Taipan showed he can win at this level with a victory five starts back, and he has distance and going experience to call on carrying 135 lb; the chief concern is whether he returns to peak form after 89 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Teed Up
runners_data.note: Has a finish-fade flag attached and ran just four days ago, a quick turnaround that rarely flatters stayers; a genuine hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield mapping by the density of similar types, his 3rd at 17f on Good is the most relevant form line but the energy reserve after a recent run is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Teed Up has run over today's trip and going before, but one unplaced effort in his last three starts makes him hard to fancy, and he ranks fifth of six on our figures — though a win four starts back and back-to-back thirds suggest he retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Uxmal
runners_data.note: OR 105 comfortably heads the ratings and is the sole confirmed front-runner — Joseph O'Brien's gelding has winning form at 14f and 22f on contrasting ground and will control the race from flag to finish; the STYLE_FIT flag notes he may be racing slightly out of his sharpest role, but as the pace-setter here he is well-placed to dictate on his own terms.
runners_data.comment: Uxmal showed his class with a win four starts back and returned to form with a third last time out, and he has experience of today's trip and going. Carrying 131 lb is the one test, but on his best he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Way Down South
runners_data.note: Gillian Scott's seven-year-old has placed form at 19f and 22f on Good-soft and is a consistent if lightly-winning hold-up type; W J Lee takes the ride and the 11-day turnaround is workable, but he has not won in his last five and needs rivals to set a genuinely strong pace to bring his staying profile into play.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with a seventh last time out and a fifth two starts back, Way Down South looks up against it here — our rating places him last of six in the field, though 11 days since his latest run at least suggests freshness, and he has experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Galileo Dame
runners_data.note: Five-year-old O'Brien second string with the 7lb claimer Pietropaolo aboard; a natural prominent type whose best effort was 2nd at 14f on Heavy and who shaped well (4th) at 18f on Good — the apprentice claim could offset the weight pull, and with a natural forward position she is the most likely horse to track Uxmal and pose a straight challenge.

races.paceDynamic: Uxmal is the one confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and should stride to the front from the off, setting a sustainable but uncontested gallop over 1m6f on Good ground at Galway. With no genuine rival willing or able to press him early, Uxmal can control tempo from the front and dictate the rhythm through the middle stages, which on Good turf typically sets up a test of staying stamina rather than a sprint finish. The hold-up trio of Taipan, Teed Up, and Way Down South will track from the rear, but with only one true pace-setter in the race, the gallop may not be strong enough to fully suit deep closers who need a truly searching test. This race shape most favours a confirmed prominent racer who can slot in just behind Uxmal and mount a sustained challenge in the straight, or Uxmal himself if he is good enough to control and quicken — the field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can all occupy their natural positions, and Counting Coup and Teed Up, both redistributed from their true roles, are unlikely to claim the ground they prefer, with Galileo Dame and Uxmal best-placed to actually secure the prominent berths at the head of affairs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uxmal Controls And Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Uxmal leads unchallenged and the pace is honest enough to expose any stamina limitations in his rivals.
scenarios.body: Uxmal dictates from the front on his own terms, covering the 1m6f on Good ground without being pressured, and if his class (OR 105, top weight) proves sufficient he simply outstays the field into the Galway straight. Galileo Dame, slotting in as the natural second prominent type, is best placed to challenge if Uxmal weakens, having shown form at this sort of trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Uxmal sets a slightly too-generous gallop and a prominent tracker times a run to pounce in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Galileo Dame or Counting Coup, tracking Uxmal through the early stages, bides its time before launching a sustained challenge from two furlongs out on the run-in. Good ground at Galway suits horses who can pick up off a steady pace, and a prominent type with a clean passage is ideally placed to benefit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the front two tie each other up, leaving the hold-up horses with a target.
scenarios.body: Taipan or Way Down South, held up in the rear early, begins to make ground from two furlongs out as the front-runners fade, with the flat Galway straight giving time for a sustained finish. Taipan's best form on Good ground (1/14f/GOO) is a relevant flag here, though his recent record is patchy and the trip requires him to be spot-on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Messy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If no horse assumes full control, the pace collapses in the middle stages and the race is decided by a chaotic sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A compressed field with no true pace advantage for any runner turns the race into a tactical lottery from the home turn, rewarding whoever gets the clearest run. Teed Up, despite a fade warning and redistribution from his natural hold-up role, could benefit if he gets a prominent tow and is not asked to make his move too early, though his recent form figures of 14/16f/GOO and 12/19f/HEA give pause.

watchPoints.text: Uxmal (front-runner) must be tracked from the start — if he gets an uncontested lead into the first turn, the race shape locks in immediately and pressure from Galileo Dame or Counting Coup in the early stages becomes the critical early flashpoint.

Taipan's 89-day absence is significant at this level; watch his pre-race market move closely, as Shane Foley booking and a known Good-ground record suggest connections may have him spot-on, but cold he is a risk in running.

Teed Up ran only four days ago and carries a finish-fade warning — monitor his early position in running; if he is prominent rather than his usual hold-up spot, he may stop quickly in the straight and become a traffic hazard for closers.

Way Down South (W J Lee) has placed form over marathon trips but not won in five; if the pace is weak this horse's staying profile may never be activated — watch whether Lee decides to push up closer than his natural hold-up role implies in an attempt to get competitive.

Galileo Dame with apprentice Pietropaolo (7lb) is a horse to monitor for market drift or support — the O'Brien yard is in excellent recent form (T14: 15/68) and if Galileo Dame is fancied she may prove the most dangerous prominent challenger to Uxmal in the straight.
